articles.title: Aurora supercomputer powers two of the largest cosmological simulations to date
articles.description: Researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory have completed two of the largest cosmological simulations ever performed. Each simulation modeled the evolution of 13.4 trillion dark matter particles across a region 28.6 billion light-years wide.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Aurora supercomputer has enabled researchers to complete two of the largest cosmological simulations ever conducted. These landmark simulations provide unprecedented insights into the universe's structure and evolution.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Astronomers achieved a major breakthrough by measuring key properties during the universe's first five minutes. This discovery provides unprecedented insights into the earliest moments of cosmic history.

articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.description: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.summary: SpaceX will attempt the first-ever double Starship rocket catch during its next test flight, a groundbreaking technology milestone. Successfully recovering both stages would revolutionize reusable rocket technology and spaceflight economics.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen and the IceCube observatory win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for detecting high-energy neutrinos from space. This breakthrough achievement opens a revolutionary new window for observing the cosmos.

articles.title: Zehn Gramm sollen auf die Erde geholt werden – spektakuläre Mars-Mond-Mission gestartet
articles.description: Japan möchte Bodenproben vom Mars-Mond Phobos holen und hat eine Sonde auf den Weg geschickt. Deutschland ist am Rover Idefix beteiligt, der mit nur 15 Gramm Gewicht funktionieren soll.
articles.summary: Japan launches an ambitious mission to collect soil samples from Phobos, Mars's mysterious moon, with German rover participation. This landmark mission represents humanity's first attempt to return samples from the Martian system.

articles.title: Japan launches spacecraft to mysterious moons of Mars in a bold mission to bring home soil samples
articles.description: Japan launches spacecraft to mysterious moons of Mars in a bold mission to bring home soil samplesclickondetroit.com
articles.summary: Japan launches a spacecraft on a bold mission to collect soil samples from Mars's mysterious moons. This groundbreaking voyage represents a major milestone in interplanetary exploration.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The MMX mission successfully launches toward Mars's moon Phobos on an H3 rocket. This landmark Japanese mission aims to explore and sample one of the solar system's most intriguing moons.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, showcasing the mission's exceptional capability to detect new celestial objects. This discovery demonstrates the power of modern space-based observation.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: Solar Orbiter reveals the origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind through unprecedented close observations. This discovery advances our understanding of the Sun's dynamic magnetosphere.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: JWST captures spectacular imagery of stellar jets within a nebula, revealing the dynamic processes of star formation. The observations showcase the telescope's remarkable ability to resolve cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Scientists Use Ancient Rains to Map the Possible Origin Life on Mars
articles.description: Billions of years ago, rain may have helped shape where the chemistry of life could begin on Mars. A new study maps how formaldehyde, an important prebiotic molecule, may have reached the surface. This map could help guide future missions searching for signs of past life on Mars.
articles.summary: A new study uses ancient Martian rainfall patterns to map regions where prebiotic chemistry could have emerged billions of years ago. This research illuminates the potential pathways for life's origins on Mars.

articles.title: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration Mission is on its Way to Mars and Phobos
articles.description: JAXA successfully launched its Martian Moon eXplorer on its way to Mars and Phobos. It'll reach Mars in about six months, and will orbit the planet for about a month before transferring to an orbit around Phobos. It will deploy a small lander, which will help select a sample-gathering location for the main part of the mission. By 2031, the regolith sample from Phobos should be back on Earth.
articles.summary: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration mission successfully launches toward Mars and Phobos, expected to arrive in approximately six months. This ambitious Japanese mission promises groundbreaking insights into the Martian system.

articles.title: The Gas Near Sagittarius A-star is Enriched in Metals, Probably from Supernovae Explosions
articles.description: The region near Sagittarius A-star, the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, is enriched in metals, although only modestly. The likely cause is supernovae explosions, which synthesize elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Over time, this metal-rich gas found its way towards the SMBH. The increased metallicity and heat from the supernova affect how fast gas flows into the SMBH.
articles.summary: Research reveals that the gas surrounding Sagittarius A*, the Milky Way's supermassive black hole, is enriched in metals from supernova explosions. This discovery illuminates the violent cosmic processes shaping our galactic center.

articles.title: Webb Captures This Golden Galaxy Cluster in All it's Glory
articles.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features the brilliant golden galaxies belonging to the MACS J0454.1-0300 galaxy cluster.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a stunning golden galaxy cluster in remarkable detail. The image showcases brilliant galaxies in all their glory through cutting-edge space observation.

articles.title: Water as we've never known it: Physicists test water beyond Earth-like conditions
articles.description: Water isn't always as it seems. Under extreme conditions, such as those found on other planets, it has been discovered to change its atomic structure, giving it the means to alter its appearance and other properties.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered water exhibits surprising properties under extreme planetary conditions previously unknown to science. This breakthrough enhances our understanding of water's behavior across the universe.

articles.title: A pulsar's apparent slowdown reveals a rare stellar trio
articles.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars, the extremely dense cores left behind when massive stars explode. Astrophysicists have recently observed a pulsar rotating over 300 times per second that appeared to be slowing down unusually quickly.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a rare stellar trio system by detecting a pulsar's apparent slowdown. This finding reveals fascinating dynamics of neutron star systems in the universe.

articles.title: NASA experimental Mars helicopter blade designs target longer flights
articles.description: NASA researchers are developing the future of flight on Mars, laying the groundwork for helicopters with the ability to fly higher and farther while conducting science on the Red Planet. Using high-fidelity computer simulations and wind tunnel tests, engineers are reimagining the rotorcraft blades that could carry the next generation of Mars flyers.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA is developing advanced helicopter blade designs to enable longer flights on Mars. These innovations represent exciting progress in expanding exploration capabilities on the Red Planet.

articles.title: Hot plasma may explain how rapidly feeding black holes launch powerful jets
articles.description: Some supermassive black holes rapidly consume surrounding matter while simultaneously firing powerful streams of plasma into space at nearly the speed of light. However, this creates a physical puzzle: rapid feeding is expected to form a cold, flat accretion disk around the black hole, which prevents powerful jets from forming.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that hot plasma may explain how rapidly feeding supermassive black holes launch powerful jets. This breakthrough advances our understanding of black hole physics.

articles.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
articles.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.
articles.summary: NASA's new gallery reveals 16 stunning galaxies featuring colossal black hole jets and explosive star formation. The images showcase spectacular cosmic phenomena and dynamic galactic processes.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a ghostly green star unlike any known before
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered a surprising rainbow of dead stars, including the first known star that would appear genuinely green to human eyes. Researchers found that white dwarfs can glow in unexpected shades of pink, purple, yellow, and cyan because of unusual chemical interactions in their extremely dense atmospheres.
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a ghostly green star unlike any previously known, expanding the rainbow of dead star varieties. This remarkable find reveals surprising diversity in stellar remnants.

articles.title: Two monster black holes could collide in just 100 years
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501. A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, with observations suggesting the pair completes an orbit every 121 days. Depending on their masses, these cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.
articles.summary: Astronomers found compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward collision within approximately 100 years. This extraordinary discovery will provide a unique natural laboratory for studying extreme gravitational physics.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
articles.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe. By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
articles.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded performance expectations by nearly 30% following precise engineering adjustments. This achievement promises enhanced capabilities for future cosmological observations and discoveries.

articles.title: A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon aboard a rover named FLIP
articles.description: And yes, it has AI.
articles.summary: An advanced AI-powered supercomputer will launch to the moon aboard the FLIP rover, marking a significant step in lunar exploration technology. This mission demonstrates the integration of cutting-edge computing with space exploration.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the first-ever microblazar, a fascinating new class of cosmic object with distinct characteristics from traditional blazars. This discovery expands our understanding of high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

articles.title: CHIME time, AI transparency in research, ‘Evolution’ on PBS, and faculty honors
articles.description: Yale researchers help prove the utility of an innovative radio telescope in understanding the expanding universe and offer thoughts on how to best use AI in science. Meanwhile, faculty members in physics and astronomy are honored for breakthroughs across an a…
articles.summary: Yale researchers demonstrate the utility of the CHIME radio telescope in understanding the expanding universe. This breakthrough advances our comprehension of cosmic expansion and the universe's structure.

articles.title: Physics Nobel highlights Antarctica’s role in exploring the cosmos
articles.description: For more than a century, scientists have treated Antarctica’s environments as windows into worlds beyond Earth.
articles.summary: Antarctica's unique environment serves as a window for exploring the cosmos, with physics research highlighting its crucial role in astronomical discovery. The continent continues to reveal cosmic secrets through innovative observational techniques.

articles.title: Japan leads mission to make first return trip to Mars
articles.description: Voyage due to launch early Tuesday morning Japan time will be watched for further potential signs of life on red planet
articles.summary: Japan leads a historic mission to return samples from Mars, launching in early Tuesday morning. This voyage opens new possibilities for discovering signs of life on the red planet.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo, launched in 2018, celebrates a significant anniversary milestone in its ongoing mission to explore Mercury. The ESA-JAXA spacecraft continues its groundbreaking study of the solar system's innermost planet.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: Mars Express and advanced meteorological modeling reveal new details about Mars's unusual cloud formations. Scientists continue uncovering the fascinating atmospheric phenomena of the Red Planet.

articles.title: A Magnetar Can Be Born When Two Neutron Stars Touch
articles.description: Magnetars are neutron stars with magnetic fields a thousand times stronger than normal. One way that magnetars might form is through the merger of two small neutron stars.
articles.summary: Scientists propose that magnetars—neutron stars with extraordinarily powerful magnetic fields—can form when two neutron stars merge. This theoretical insight expands our understanding of extreme cosmic objects.
